forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Yorkshire told PWLB loan rates are forecast to fall to 4.3–4.9% over three years
news_drafts.lead:
South Yorkshire's Audit, Standards and Risk Committee received a quarterly update on its treasury management, meaning how the council borrows, invests spare cash and manages the risks of both, at its meeting on 8 October 2026. It included its advisers' forecast for the cost of borrowing from the Public Works Loan Board (PWLB), the government's lending arm for councils and where most council borrowing comes from.

The paper says PWLB rates are currently around 5.6% to 6.1%, depending on the length of the loan. In its words, they "are expected to gradually reduce" to between 4.3% and 4.9% over the next three years.

The forecasts are the treasury advisers' own, dated 21 September 2026. They have Bank Rate, the Bank of England's main interest rate, rising from 3.75% to 4.00% by December. The direction after that is described as "evenly balanced".

findings.headline: Staff ethical conduct survey (165 respondents) shows 66.3% positive awareness overall but only 47.4% positive on whistleblowing; training scored 31.6% positive for whistleblowing
findings.detail: Survey of 165 staff on ethical conduct awareness found 66.3% positive response overall. Conflicts of interest scored highest at 78.5% positive; whistleblowing scored lowest at 47.4% positive. Training was identified as consistent weakness: whistleblowing training only 31.6% positive, Code of Conduct training 40.1% positive. Qualitative feedback emphasized need for regular refresher training and improved access to guidance.
findings.matters: Weak whistleblowing culture and confidence could prevent identification of problems; training gaps suggest awareness and knowledge are not embedded or sustained, affecting overall control environment.
findings.figures: 165 respondents; 66.3% overall positive; 47.4% whistleblowing positive; 31.6% whistleblowing training positive; 40.1% Code of Conduct training positive
findings.quote: Whistleblowing was the weakest area, with only 47.4% of responses being positive. Training was the weakest scoring element across each of the four areas, with whistleblowing particularly low at 31.6% positive.

findings.headline: Contracts Register published by authority last updated May 2025, containing 131 contracts with historic end dates
findings.detail: MCA's Transparency Tracker requires Contracts Register to be updated quarterly. Version on website last updated May 2025 (over 16 months prior to audit). Audit identified 131 contracts recorded with end dates prior to review date. Register does not distinguish between active and archived contracts, reducing clarity of public information on current contractual commitments.
findings.matters: Failure to maintain required public register indicates weak asset management and contract lifecycle control; suggests organizational compliance and process discipline issues.
findings.figures: Last updated May 2025; 131 contracts with historic end dates identified
findings.quote: the version available on the MCA's website was last updated in May 2025. Our review of the published register identified numerous contracts with historic end dates, with review of the published contracts register identifying 131 contracts recorded with end dates prior to the date of our review.

findings.headline: Eight management actions agreed to strengthen ethical conduct framework, five medium priority, all due 31 March 2027
findings.detail: Audit identified areas where existing ethical conduct arrangements could be enhanced. Five medium priority actions were agreed to establish: dedicated training on conflicts of interest and gifts/hospitality; centralized gifts and hospitality workflow with approval audit trail; clear thresholds and approval criteria for gifts and hospitality; and strengthened monitoring of outstanding annual interest declarations. Three low priority actions address whistleblowing register, lessons learned process, and refresher training programme.
findings.matters: Internal audit findings on control environment weaknesses indicate governance issues that affect decision-making quality and procurement oversight.
findings.figures: 5 medium priority, 3 low priority, all due 31 March 2027
findings.quote: As a result, we have agreed five medium priority and three low priority management actions.

findings.headline: Health and safety incident procedure documentation: revised version still pending approval as of 16 September, with 30 September deadline
findings.detail: The procedure for recording, logging, investigating and resolving health and safety incidents was revised following audit findings but required further amendments. As of the report date, a revised document had been completed and was scheduled for presentation to the Document Standards Group on 29 September 2026 for approval, with a final deadline of 30 September 2026.
findings.matters: Absence of current approved procedures creates ambiguity about incident handling processes and can result in inconsistent investigation standards and incomplete audit trails
findings.figures: Original implementation deadline: April 2026; current deadline: 30 September 2026
findings.quote: A revised procedure was presented to our Document Standards Group (DSG) in May 2026 but was found to require further review and amendments as there were key elements which had not been included. A revised document has now been completed and will be presented to DSG on 29 September 2026.

findings.headline: GDPR information asset register remains incomplete despite annual assurance refresh process
findings.detail: The Cyber Resilience and Information Governance Manager circulated instructions requiring asset owners to review and complete all Information Asset Register fields as part of the annual refresh. Audit testing confirmed that multiple entries continue to contain blank fields or placeholders. Management acknowledged full completion by staff has not yet been achieved, though wider information management strategy work is expected to improve this.
findings.matters: A complete register is required for GDPR compliance and data protection risk management; incomplete records mean the authority lacks full visibility of its information assets, data flows, and processing activities
findings.figures: No specific completion percentage given, but issue confirmed as ongoing
findings.quote: However, some records continued to contain blank fields or placeholders. The Head of Corporate Governance confirmed that some fields remain incomplete and that full completion by staff has not yet been achieved, but ongoing work around a wider information management strategy should help this.
